messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: P0 - cache storm detected on kv-store cluster kV-eu-west-1. Error rates and latencies spiking. Paging oncall SRE.

devon: seeing 5xx spike on /v1/generate starting ~1875001200. 99th latency from 120ms -> 4.2s. Root cause hints in kv-metrics: kv-put queue length skyrocketed.

liam: digging into runtime logs now. Also correlating batcher metric — continuous-batcher.pending_batches_count jumped 10x.

maya: customer telemetry: several customers report streaming disconnects and truncated responses. CS ticket CS-1420 opened (high priority).

devon: immediate mitigation attempt: disable continuous batching for hostpool alpha via feature-flag. command: `PATCH /flags/continuous_batching?env=alpha` -> roll=true -> false.

deploy-bot: feature-flag update applied to alpha hosts: continuous_batching=false (1875001324).

liam: after disabling, pending_batches_count halved but kv-store write amplification still high. digging cache keys now.

eva: logs show a ton of unique prefix keys created by prompt-template pipeline. Looks like template renderer started inserting ephemeral user tokens into prefix used for KV. cause: template drift after a change in the templating lib.

sam: are these new prefix keys causing TTL churn? if keys never match, prefix cache stops hitting and writes explode.

devon: exactly. I see prefix hash entropy increased sharply at 1875001100. Tokenizer version mismatch between runtime (v3.1) and promptgen (v3.2-alpha).

maya: oh nice find — promptgen 3.2 introduced a normalization step that changes whitespace handling for templated prefixes. That will change the hash.

ashley: customer impact estimate: ~120k requests affected in the last hour, errors ~3.4% on hosted API endpoints for text-gen. Potentially longer for customers pinned to dedicated pools using same runtime stack.

liam: propose immediate rollback of promptgen to 3.1 on prod config and a targeted KV prefix prune for malformed prefixes. Plan: 1) rollback promptgen rollout -> 3.1 2) run prefix-compact and delete keys matching regex `pg:tmp:*` 3) re-enable controlled batching with lowered batch size.

devon: I'm taking command. Rolling back promptgen now (1875002010). ETA ~6m for full rollout across control-plane.

deploy-bot: rollback started: promptgen -> 3.1 (canary 1875002075).

liam: meanwhile I'll run a dry-run of the prefix deletion on staging. Command we plan to run on prod: `kv-tool delete --prefix "pg:tmp:" --dry-run=false --concurrency=8`. We'll throttle to avoid thundering.

eva: note: do NOT delete prefixes that start with `pg:perm:` — those are real templates for long-running sessions. We only want ephemeral keys that were created by the drift. Regex: `^pg:tmp:[0-9a-f]{12}`.

maya: rolling temporary batch cap to 8 tokens for all hostpools to reduce write amplification: config change applied (1875002940).

devon: promptgen rollback complete across control plane (1875003124). Early metrics: prefix hit-rate improving, KV writes dropping.

liam: kicking off the controlled prefix delete now with concurrency=4 and backoff windows. Monitoring closely.

deploy-bot: kv-tool job started (job-id: kv-clean-1875003210).

eva: after first 10k deletions we see KV write rate down ~48% and error rate falling to 0.9%. still watching tail latencies.

sam: customer comms draft: "We've identified a caching regression due to a templating change that increased prefix churn, causing transient errors and latency. We rolled back the templating change, pruned ephemeral cache keys, and applied temporary batching limits. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause and mitigation plan." Feedback?

maya: fine. add estimated window (approx 1875001100 - 1875003000) and affected endpoints list (`/v1/generate`, `/v1/chat/stream`).

devon: agree. Also add mitigation steps we took. Sending to CS now.

ashley: handoff: devon continuing post-mortem. liam will stabilize kv cleanup and eva will validate no data loss. I'll coordinate customer follow-ups. If anything regresses, page me first.

devon: leaving a runbook entry: - watch kv-put-queue, - check prefix-hash-entropy, - verify tokenizer versions across services before rollout.

liam: kv-clean job finished (1875004520). Final numbers: 146,842 ephemeral keys removed, sustained KV write rate down 55%, 99th latency back to 180ms.

eva: I validated no perm keys deleted, session continuity tests pass.

devon: closing mitigation. Moving to postmortem phase. Will open incident report and include diffs for templating lib and rollout gating improvements.

pagerbot: Incident transitioned to postmortem state (1875007567).
